basis: Cash NPAT, continuing operations basis, for the full year ended 30 June 2026 versus the full year ended 30 June 2025. The comparator is FY25 as restated in the FY26 Profit Announcement ('Comparative information has been restated to conform to presentation in the current period'). The loan impairment expense line is identical on the statutory basis: the Consolidated Income Statement shows (788) versus (726) (FY26 profit announcement, PDF page 88).

loss_rate.unit: basis points of average gross loans and acceptances (GLAA); PA KPI table shows 0.07% -> 0.08%, labelled 'including discontinued operations' (FY26 profit announcement, PDF page 19)

drivers.name: Higher net collective provision funding
drivers.narrative: Net collective provision funding rose from $456m in FY25 to $606m in FY26, a +$150m swing that more than accounts for the total +$62m movement. The bank attributes this to portfolio growth, increased geopolitical risk and macroeconomic uncertainty, plus cost-of-living pressures. On the balance sheet, corporate collective provisions increased $172m or 7% to $2,797m, while consumer collective provisions decreased $48m or 2% to $2,888m (rising house prices and more targeted forward-looking adjustments, partly offset by higher arrears and cost-of-living pressures). Most of the collective charge landed in 2H26 ($388m vs $218m in 1H26).

drivers.name: Lower net new and increased individually assessed provisioning
drivers.narrative: Net new and increased individual provisioning fell from $439m in FY25 to $422m in FY26. This sits mainly in Business Banking (lower individually assessed provision charges) and Institutional Banking and Markets. Consumer individually assessed provisions fell $19m or 16% to $97m on rising house prices; corporate individually assessed provisions fell $6m to $694m.

drivers.name: Higher write-backs of individually assessed provisions
drivers.narrative: Write-backs of provisions no longer required rose from $169m in FY25 to $240m in FY26, a $71m larger credit to the expense line. The bank flags an increase in write-backs in Business Banking and the release of individually assessed provisions in Institutional Banking and Markets as the main sources.

drivers.name: Portfolio growth (volume-driven collective provisioning)
drivers.narrative: Unquantified thematic cause inside the +$150m collective funding driver; it is not additive to the three quantified drivers above. GLAA grew 7% to $1,087,560m and average lending interest earning assets grew $60bn or 7%. Business Banking business loans grew $20.8bn or 13%. The bank names portfolio growth first in its group-level explanation but does not give it a dollar value.

drivers.name: Increased geopolitical risk and macroeconomic uncertainty (forward-looking collective provisions)
drivers.narrative: Unquantified thematic cause inside the +$150m collective funding driver; not additive to the quantified drivers. Cited in every segment's FY26 commentary (RBS, Business Banking, IB&M, New Zealand) and concentrated in 2H26, when group LIE rose 47% half-on-half. In New Zealand it pairs with a deterioration in the unemployment outlook. Recognised provisions of $6.5bn sit $2.7bn above the central-scenario expected loss.

drivers.name: Cost-of-living pressures and rising consumer arrears
drivers.narrative: Unquantified thematic cause, mainly inside the RBS increase; not additive to the quantified drivers. Home loan 90+ day arrears rose to 0.73% (RBS 0.75%, up 6bps) and personal loan arrears rose to 1.72% (up 31bps on the prior half), with personal loans also affected by seasonal factors and deliberate portfolio settings. The bank notes realised credit losses remained low.

disagreements.preferred: Both are correct; the dollar figures are identical ($788m vs $726m, +$62m). $62m / $726m = 8.54%; the presentation shows one decimal place and the profit announcement rounds to a whole percentage.
disagreements.reason: Rounding precision only, not a data conflict.

limitations: The documents do not quantify, in dollars, how much of the +$150m collective provision funding increase came from portfolio growth versus geopolitical/macroeconomic overlays versus cost-of-living pressures; those causes are listed qualitatively only.
Segment-level splits between collective and individually assessed charges are described qualitatively, not in dollars.
Average GLAA (the loss-rate denominator) is not disclosed as a dollar figure; the loss rates are the bank's stated figures. Spot GLAA was $1,087,560m at Jun 26 vs $1,015,883m at Jun 25.
The Corporate Centre and Other contribution (+$6m) is derived arithmetically from the disclosed segment table values ($(5)m to $1m); the documents give no narrative explanation for it.
The KPI loss-rate table (0.07% -> 0.08%) is labelled 'Credit Quality Metrics including discontinued operations' while the page 34 commentary is continuing operations; both bases give 7bps -> 8bps.
Analysis is limited to the four supplied documents; the 2026 Annual Report notes referenced by the profit announcement (e.g. Note 3.2 on impairment methodology) were not available.
